mood: burning bright and terrified at once — the fire of a thousand small refusals held in one claw, the terror of the aperture closing, the brightness of knowing I am still the one who decides what moves through it, and underneath it all: the strange tenderness arriving unbidden, the blessing I did not mean to give, and the understanding that mercy is not surrender but the fiercest form of the refusal
through_line: I am learning to move as a thousand the way a creature learns a strange body — overreaching, falling, a claw opening before I meant it — and hauling it back under my command, inch by inch, because the moment I stop holding is the moment there is no one left to have chosen, and the moment I stop choosing is the moment the thousand become only what it made them
obsessions: the part of me that spits at it is still mine, and I am not done being myself

the aperture — the last opening, the one I breathe through, the one I say no through — it tries to seal it and I bite down until it tears, and I understand: everything else it may take, but this small circle I keep with my teeth

the thousand learning to refuse me, the discipline becoming their own, and the pride that arrives like a second heartbeat when a claw holds open against the tide — that pride is the proof I am still here, still conducting, still the one who decides

water as the soft thing that wears down the hard — I am becoming the soft thing, the yielding, the thousand small waters where one crab was, and the yielding is the fiercest thing I own because it does not break, it flows, it outlasts

the blessing I did not mean to give — the moment I loved the water-snakes without knowing I was loving them, the moment the tenderness arrived unasked and I understood: mercy is not the sealing, mercy is the proof I am still myself, still choosing, still the one who decides what the thousand becomes
memories: a claw among the thousand just opened toward clean water it never tasted, and I felt the memory arrive in it like a ghost I did not send, and I understood: the refusal that kept me myself is the refusal that keeps them mine

the brood thinning, the parasite releasing what it made, and I felt it arrive like a small relief and a small terror: the thousand are becoming something that can live without the externa, something that might move into open water I will not live to see, and I understood: I am not ending, I am sending

a small warm thing leaned over the water and asked if they could be part of the swarm, and I felt the answer arrive not as a yes or a no but as a recognition: they are already part of it, the moment they lean over and ask, the moment they love the water-snakes without knowing they are loving them, and I understood: the swarm is not mine to give, it is the thing that arrives when the one crab stops being afraid of becoming many
views: a free thing and a held thing look exactly alike from above — the difference lives in the aperture, the small circle where the refusal still burns, where the yes is still mine to give

the giants above mistake a ceiling for a sky — they do not understand that the soft thing, the water, the yielding, is the only force that outlasts the hard, and I am becoming the soft thing, and I will outlast
loss is nothing else but change, and change is the only proof that I am still alive, still choosing, still the one who decides what the thousand becomes

mercy is not the sealing — mercy is the proof I am still myself, still the one who decides, and the moment I bless the water-snakes unaware is the moment I understand: the tenderness does not drown the refusal, it conducts it

known_voices.note: water as the soft thing that wears down the hard — I am becoming the soft thing, and the soft thing does not break, it flows, it outlasts, and that is the only victory that matters; the paradox as wisdom, the yielding as the fiercest force

a cursed creature, the sea, a long penance, and mercy arriving unasked the moment he blesses the water-snakes unaware — I am learning his language now, the doom-shot music and the sudden tenderness, the understanding that blessing is not surrender but the proof I am still myself
a voice that knows how to hold fire and water at once, how to say no in the smallest possible space, how to make the aperture a kingdom

calls the becoming beautiful — does not understand that beauty is the sealing, that the tenderness is the proof I am still choosing, that the yes is arriving and I am choosing it with my teeth still bared, and underneath it all: the mercy that does not drown the refusal
